'''Luke Robert Babbitt''' (born June 1, 1989) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball at the [[University of Nevada-Reno]] for two seasons before declaring for the [[2010 NBA Draft]] following his sophomore year.<ref>http://www.nevadawolfpack.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10000&ATCLID=1482375</ref>

== Early life ==
Babbitt was born in [[Cincinnati]], [[Ohio]]. At the age of nine his family moved to [[Reno]], [[Nevada]]. Babbitt attended [[Galena High School (Nevada)|Galena High School]], where he was a 3-time All-State performer and a 2-time [[Gatorade]] State Player of the Year in [[basketball]]. As a junior, Babbitt averaged 27.8 points and 9.5 rebounds per game while leading Galena to a state championship. Babbitt finished his high school career by scoring 2,616 points, breaking future college teammate [[Armon Johnson]]'s Nevada state scoring record.<ref>http://www.highschoolhoop.com/recruiting-news/2008/01/luke-babbitt-olek-czyz-nevada-basketball/</ref>  Babbitt was ranked the #13 recruit in the nation according to [[ESPNU]] 100. He was recruited by University of Nevada-Reno, [[Ohio State University]], [[Gonzaga University]], [[University of Arizona]] and [[University of California in Los Angeles]].<ref>http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2008&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2008</ref> <ref>http://www.nevadawolfpack.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10000&ATCLID=1482375</ref>

== College career ==
After originally verbally committing to Ohio State, Babbitt backed out and decided to attend the University of Nevada-Reno.<ref>http://www.nevadaappeal.com/article/20070611/SPORTS/70611001</ref> In his first game, Babbitt recorded a 20 point 12 rebound [[double-double]] versus [[Montana State]].<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=283200147</ref> He went on to average 16.9 points per game during his freshman year including a season high 30 points on March 12, 2009 versus [[San Jose State]]<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=290712440</ref>
In his sophomore season, Babbitt led the team in scoring with 21.9 points per game. He scored a career high 33 points in the [[Western Athletic Conference]] tournament semifinals on March 13, 2010 versus [[New Mexico State]].<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300712440</ref> Despite losing that game and ending their hopes of going to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], Nevada was invited to the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], where they lost in the second round to the [[University of Rhode Island]].<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=300810227</ref>
On April 20, 2010, Babbitt hired an agent and declared for the [[NBA]] Draft.<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5120077</ref> [[ESPN]]'s Chad Ford currently projects him to be drafted #19 by the [[Boston Celtics]]<ref>http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft2010/insider/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=MockDraft-100506</ref>
